title: Delete Characters to Make Fancy String
spaceBreakdown:
- string result: holds the output (not counted as auxiliary by LeetCode convention)
- loop variables: O(1)
- not counted: input s, returned result
approach: Scan left to right, building the answer character by character. For each character, append it unless doing so would create three identical consecutive characters - i.e., the last two characters already in the answer are both equal to it. This keeps exactly two characters from every run of three or more, which is optimal since any run longer than two must be trimmed to at most two.
hints: When a run of identical letters is longer than two, how many of them can the final string actually keep? The constraint n ≤ 10^5 means a single left-to-right pass is the right budget.

Build the answer one character at a time and reject a character only when the last two characters already in the answer match it. For "leeetcode", the third 'e' is skipped because the answer already ends in "ee".

```
result = empty
for each char c in s:
    if length(result) >= 2
       and result[-1] == c
       and result[-2] == c:
        skip c
    else:
        append c to result
return result
```

**Single character** - smallest allowed input has no triples to remove.
`Input: s = "a"` → `Expected: "a"`
⚠️ Bug: checking `result[-1] == c && result[-2] == c` without guarding `length >= 2` → undefined behavior / crash on this input.

**All identical** - every character after the second must be dropped.
`Input: s = "aaaaa"` → `Expected: "aa"`
⚠️ Bug: comparing only `result[-1] == c` (one character) instead of two → returns `"a"`, deleting one too many.

**Already fancy** - no deletions needed; the answer equals the input.
`Input: s = "aab"` → `Expected: "aab"`
⚠️ Bug: same single-character comparison bug → returns `"ab"`, wrongly dropping the second 'a'.

**Run at the very end** - the trimming must apply to trailing runs, not just leading ones.
`Input: s = "aaabaaaa"` → `Expected: "aabaa"`
⚠️ Bug: only scanning until the first triple and stopping → returns `"aabaaaa"`, leaving the trailing run untouched.

followUps.q: Generalize to "no k consecutive equal characters" for arbitrary k ≥ 2.
followUps.a: Keep a counter for the current run length instead of checking the last two characters. Append c only when the current run length is below k-1; otherwise skip. Time stays O(n), space O(1).

followUps.q: The input arrives as an unbounded stream you cannot store entirely; emit the fancy string online.
followUps.a: Keep only the last kept character and its current run length. Emit c when run < 2, otherwise drop it and do not increment the run. Memory is O(1) regardless of stream length; time is O(n).

followUps.q: Return the minimum number of deletions instead of the resulting string.
followUps.a: For each run of identical characters of length L, it contributes max(0, L - 2) deletions. Sum these over all runs in one pass. Time O(n), space O(1).
